react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolites form a cohesive biological signal centred on tryptophan metabolism, with convergent evidence from three independent paradigms. RaMP ORA (multi-database, FDR 8.86 × 10⁻¹⁹, 7/9 input metabolites) and MetaboAnalystR PSEA (KEGG-only, p = 5.41 × 10⁻⁹, 6 metabolites) both identify KEGG:hsa00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' as the top-ranked pathway. The m/z-direct mummichog algorithm independently recovers the same pathway as its top hit (p = 0.000252, 9 matched network nodes) without requiring ID resolution, confirming the signal is robust to annotation quality. WikiPathways additionally captures three tightly related sub-pathways: the IDO metabolic pathway (FDR 8.38 × 10⁻⁹), the kynurenine branch feeding NAD⁺ biosynthesis (WP:WP4210, FDR 5.82 × 10⁻¹¹; WP:WP2485, FDR 6.80 × 10⁻⁸), and the serotonin/melatonin biosynthesis module in Reactome (FDR 2.02 × 10⁻⁸). L-Tryptophan (KEGG:C00078) is the upstream driver substrate, giving rise to two downstream branches: the biogenic-amine arm producing tryptamine, serotonin and melatonin, and the kynurenine arm producing 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid and quinolinic acid. The detection of both arms simultaneously, with high fold-enrichment (875–1175×) and 6–7 metabolites per pathway, indicates a broad perturbation of tryptophan catabolism rather than a single enzymatic step. Ureidosuccinic acid (C00438) and O-phosphoethanolamine (C00346) do not fall on the tryptophan core and likely reflect independent pyrimidine/glycerophospholipid signals.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolites form a cohesive biological signal centred on tryptophan metabolism, with convergent evidence from three independent paradigms. RaMP ORA (multi-database, FDR 8.86 × 10⁻¹⁹, 7/9 input metabolites) and MetaboAnalystR PSEA (KEGG-only, p = 5.41 × 10⁻⁹, 6 metabolites) both identify KEGG:hsa00380 'Tryptophan metabolism' as the top-ranked pathway. The m/z-direct mummichog algorithm independently recovers the same pathway as its top hit (p = 0.000252, 9 matched network nodes) without requiring ID resolution, confirming the signal is robust to annotation quality. WikiPathways additionally captures three tightly related sub-pathways: the IDO metabolic pathway (FDR 8.38 × 10⁻⁹), the kynurenine branch feeding NAD⁺ biosynthesis (WP:WP4210, FDR 5.82 × 10⁻¹¹; WP:WP2485, FDR 6.80 × 10⁻⁸), and the serotonin/melatonin biosynthesis module in Reactome (FDR 2.02 × 10⁻⁸). L-Tryptophan (KEGG:C00078) is the upstream driver substrate, giving rise to two downstream branches: the biogenic-amine arm producing tryptamine, serotonin and melatonin, and the kynurenine arm producing 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid and quinolinic acid. The detection of both arms simultaneously, with high fold-enrichment (875–1175×) and 6–7 metabolites per pathway, indicates a broad perturbation of tryptophan catabolism rather than a single enzymatic step. Ureidosuccinic acid (C00438) and O-phosphoethanolamine (C00346) do not fall on the tryptophan core and likely reflect independent pyrimidine/glycerophospholipid signals.
